info.title: Ryu Messaging API
info.summary: Hosted SMS, MMS, voice messages, WhatsApp and phone numbers over AWS End User Messaging, billed at cost from organization credits.
info.description: Ryu Messaging is early access on the Ryu control plane. Ryu enables it for each organization, and the organization's Ryu Messaging feature must also be on: until both are, organization routes answer `404 not_found` or `403 feature_disabled`. There is no self-hosted Messaging service. Authenticate with a `ryu_` API key in `x-api-key`; it needs the `messaging:read` scope to read and `messaging:manage` to send, buy numbers or change settings, and a personal key also sends `X-Ryu-Organization`. Every send and number purchase holds the quoted ceiling on the organization's credit first and settles at the AWS price, so those writes require an `Idempotency-Key`. Prices are AWS End User Messaging's own, with no Ryu markup; this document states no prices. Every refusal is `{error, message, ...}` (`MessagingError`).

servers.description: Early access on the documented control-plane host: Messaging answers here only for organizations where Ryu has enabled it and the organization has turned on Ryu Messaging; use the control-plane origin Ryu gave you if it differs.

post.description: What Messaging POSTs to the organization's `webhookUrl` (`PUT /orgs/{orgId}/settings`). Verify `webhook-signature` with the `whsec_` secret from the settings reply or `POST /orgs/{orgId}/settings/webhook-secret/rotate`; the headers are repeated as `svix-id`, `svix-timestamp` and `svix-signature`. Each event is delivered at most once, with up to three attempts a few hundred milliseconds apart and no durable retry queue, so reconcile with `GET /orgs/{orgId}/messages` after an outage.

parameters.name: webhook-id
parameters.description: The event id (`event_id`). A retry of the same delivery keeps it; deduplicate on it.

parameters.name: webhook-timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds when this attempt was sent. Reject a delivery whose timestamp is far from your clock (the Standard Webhooks libraries allow five minutes).

parameters.name: webhook-signature
parameters.description: `v1,` and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<raw body>`, keyed with the base64-decoded part of the `whsec_` secret after the prefix. Compare in constant time; the Standard Webhooks and Svix libraries verify it.

200.description: Any 2xx acknowledges the delivery; another status or a timeout counts as a failed attempt.

ApiKey.name: x-api-key
ApiKey.description: A `ryu_` organization or personal API key with a `messaging:read` or `messaging:manage` scope. Send `X-Ryu-Organization` with a personal key.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: Required on every send and number purchase (`400 idempotency_key_required` without it). Up to 255 characters, scoped to the organization and the operation, kept for 24 hours. The same key and body replay the first response with its status and charge nothing again; a different body gets `409 idempotency_key_reused`; a repeat while the first request runs gets `409 idempotency_in_progress`. A send refused before or by AWS (a 4xx, `402`, `429`, `502 provider_refused` or `502 media_upload_failed`) releases the key, so a later request with it is a new attempt. Messaging sends no `Idempotent-Replayed` header.

OrgId.description: The organization. An organization API key must belong to it; a personal key must also name it in `X-Ryu-Organization`.

XRyuOrganization.name: X-Ryu-Organization

Sunset.description: Present only on a deprecated route with a removal date: the HTTP-date after which it may stop responding (RFC 8594).

Link.description: On a deprecated route, `rel="deprecation"` links the versioning and deprecation policy (RFC 9745 §3) and `rel="successor-version"` the replacement.
